note: Scripture authority is the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0), bundled as library/data/bible/owb-am-b.json.gz and read offline (owb-am). Every Scripture quotation in this book was re-quoted to it verbatim (founder decision, 2026-11-18: Amharic quotes OWB everywhere), replacing the 1962/2003 UBS New Testament wording the first edition carried and the Old Testament wording it had self-rendered or borrowed from other shipped Amharic works; the UBS credit line this file once owed is no longer owed for this work.

A `mined` row is a verbatim OWB span in that block: the whole verse, verses joined, the shortest contiguous span carrying the quoted clause, or exact OWB pieces joined with '…' (Ephesians 4:13, Acts 6:4 in chapter 19); a verbatim recitation without quote marks counts (founder rule, 2026-11-19) — the good shepherd (John 10:11), «the man of sorrows» (Isaiah 53:3), «God is love» (1 John 4:8), and the Scripture Alexander Knox recites (Luke 24:32, James 1:27, Acts 26:25). The chapter titles «ብቃታችን ከእግዚአብሔር ነው» and «ፊደል ይገድላል» are OWB's own words (2 Corinthians 3:5, 3:6). `self_rendered` rows each carry a `why`: allusions and the author's own paraphrases left as prose, many of them inside the words of the men Bounds quotes.

Judgement calls: Matthew 11:12 — Canon Liddon applies the AV's «the violent take it by force» to importunate prayer, while OWB reads the opposite sense (the kingdom suffers attack and violent men try to seize it); the clause is rendered from the English and marked self_rendered. Psalm 63:1 — McCheyne's «Early will I seek thee» is quoted as OWB has it («አጥብቄም እሻሃለሁ», earnestly), the paired Psalm 5:3 («ጎሕ ሲቀድ ድምፄን ትሰማለህ») carrying his point about the morning. Luke 18:7 — OWB makes the AV's question a statement, so the quotation runs on into OWB's own question «እነርሱን ለመርዳት ይዘገያልን?», which keeps Bounds's «asks». Paul's «My gospel» is quoted as OWB words it at Romans 16:25 («ወንጌሌ»). Acts 9:6, Psalm 68:31 and the critical-text verses do not occur in this book.
